title: One Tissue, Two Axons, One Receptor

scenes.tts: Sema three A is made in the ventral cord. Pain fibres stay out, and muscle afferents go in. Is the difference in the cue, or in the axons?
scenes.caption: Sema3A is made in the ventral cord. Pain fibres stay out, and muscle afferents go in. Is the difference in the cue, or in the axons?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Tissue, Two Axons, One Receptor. Cross-section with the ventral cord shaded for Sema3A; red axon stops, blue axon enters. Question on screen: cue or axon?
scenes.narration: Sema3A is made in the ventral cord. Pain fibres stay out, and muscle afferents go in. Is the difference in the cue, or in the axons?

scenes.tts: Here is the test. Set a dorsal root ganglion in a collagen gel, beside a piece of ventral cord.
scenes.visual: A collagen gel with a round dorsal root ganglion explant on the left and a piece of ventral spinal cord on the right.
scenes.narration: Here is the test. Set a dorsal root ganglion in a collagen gel, beside a piece of ventral cord.

scenes.tts: Grow it once with nerve growth factor, and once with neurotrophin three. The medium largely decides which neurons grow.
scenes.caption: Grow it once with nerve growth factor (NGF), and once with neurotrophin-3 (NT-3). The medium largely decides which neurons grow.
scenes.visual: Two copies of the dish side by side. Medium labels: NGF on the left, NT-3 on the right.
scenes.narration: Grow it once with nerve growth factor (NGF), and once with neurotrophin-3 (NT-3). The medium largely decides which neurons grow.

scenes.tts: Where will the axons grow in each dish?
scenes.visual: Both explants, no axons yet. Question on screen: where will the axons grow?
scenes.narration: Where will the axons grow in each dish?

scenes.tts: With nerve growth factor, the pain fibres grow. They grow poorly on the side facing the cord. The ring of axons, the halo, is lopsided.
scenes.caption: With NGF, the pain fibres grow. They grow poorly on the side facing the cord. The ring of axons, the halo, is lopsided.
scenes.visual: NGF dish: red axons sprout long on the far side and short on the near side. Label: asymmetric halo. On screen, made-up numbers: near 150, far 600, ratio 0.25.
scenes.narration: With NGF, the pain fibres grow. They grow poorly on the side facing the cord. The ring of axons, the halo, is lopsided.

scenes.tts: With neurotrophin three, the muscle afferents grow. Their halo is nearly round.
scenes.caption: With NT-3, the muscle afferents grow. Their halo is nearly round.
scenes.visual: NT-3 dish: blue axons sprout almost evenly all round. On screen, made-up numbers: near 540, far 600, ratio 0.9.
scenes.narration: With NT-3, the muscle afferents grow. Their halo is nearly round.

scenes.tts: Same tissue, two answers. Messersmith, Kolodkin and colleagues found this pattern in rat explants. Cells secreting Sema three A did the same.
scenes.caption: Same tissue, two answers. Messersmith, Kolodkin and colleagues found this pattern in rat explants. Cells secreting Sema3A did the same.
scenes.visual: Both halos side by side. Label: Messersmith and colleagues, 1995. A third dish swaps the cord for cells secreting Sema3A and gives the same two halos.
scenes.narration: Same tissue, two answers. Messersmith, Kolodkin and colleagues found this pattern in rat explants. Cells secreting Sema3A did the same.

scenes.tts: So how does a growth cone hear Sema three A? Two groups found the receptor independently. It was neuropilin.
scenes.caption: So how does a growth cone hear Sema3A? Two groups found the receptor independently. It was neuropilin.
scenes.visual: A growth cone membrane. A neuropilin molecule drawn as a catcher's mitt holds Sema3A. Label: neuropilin, 1997, two groups.
scenes.narration: So how does a growth cone hear Sema3A? Two groups found the receptor independently. It was neuropilin.

scenes.tts: Neuropilin binds Sema three A tightly. But its tail inside the cell is short, with nothing like an enzyme. Where is the wire?
scenes.caption: Neuropilin binds Sema3A tightly. But its tail inside the cell is short, with nothing like an enzyme. Where is the wire?
scenes.visual: Zoom on neuropilin's tiny inner tail, about forty amino acids, ending in nothing. Question on screen: where is the wire?
scenes.narration: Neuropilin binds Sema3A tightly. But its tail inside the cell is short, with nothing like an enzyme. Where is the wire?

scenes.tts: Two more groups pointed to the plexins. These membrane proteins have a large part inside the cell.
scenes.visual: A plexin appears beside neuropilin, with a long wire running into the cell. Label: plexins, 1999.
scenes.narration: Two more groups pointed to the plexins. These membrane proteins have a large part inside the cell.

scenes.tts: In engineered cells, neuropilin alone binds the cue, but the cell does not respond. With plexin as well, binding is tighter. Now the cells shrink and round up.
scenes.visual: A table builds row by row: cells carry / binds? / responds? Neither: no, no. Neuropilin-1 alone: yes, no. Plexin-A1 alone: little or none, no. Both: yes, more tightly; yes, cells round up.
scenes.narration: In engineered cells, neuropilin alone binds the cue, but the cell does not respond. With plexin as well, binding is tighter. Now the cells shrink and round up.

scenes.tts: Other work tested neurons, which keep their other receptor parts. There, a neuropilin with no inner tail still let growth cones collapse.
scenes.visual: A separate inset, not a row of the engineered-cell table. Label: neurons, other work; their other receptor parts intact. Neuropilin lacking its tail: binds yes; growth cones still collapse.
scenes.narration: Other work tested neurons, which keep their other receptor parts. There, a neuropilin with no inner tail still let growth cones collapse.

scenes.tts: Now give sensory neurons extra plexin with its inner part cut off. They still have their own normal plexin. What happens?
scenes.visual: The neuron inset gains a second row with its final cell blank: sensory neurons plus extra plexin lacking its inner part: binds, expected; responds ?
scenes.narration: Now give sensory neurons extra plexin with its inner part cut off. They still have their own normal plexin. What happens?

scenes.tts: The response is blocked. The broken plexin interferes with the cell's own working receptors. One likely idea: it joins neuropilin and the cue in complexes that cannot signal.
scenes.visual: The blank fills: no, response blocked. Animation labelled possible mechanism: some Sema3A-neuropilin complexes pair with broken plexins that have no wire, and those complexes send no signal.
scenes.narration: The response is blocked. The broken plexin interferes with the cell's own working receptors. One likely idea: it joins neuropilin and the cue in complexes that cannot signal.

scenes.tts: A mutant that blocks the normal protein this way is called a dominant negative. So neuropilin catches, and plexin signals.
scenes.visual: Label: dominant negative. Summary on screen: neuropilin catches; plexin signals.
scenes.narration: A mutant that blocks the normal protein this way is called a dominant negative. So neuropilin catches, and plexin signals.

scenes.tts: Inside, the plexin switches off a small G T Pase of the Ras family. That protein helps integrins grip the surface. Other plexin pathways act on actin and microtubules. Together, the growth cone loses grip and actin.
scenes.caption: Inside, the plexin switches off a small GTPase of the Ras family. That protein helps integrins grip the surface. Other plexin pathways act on actin and microtubules. Together, the growth cone loses grip and actin.
scenes.visual: Inside the growth cone, two branches from the plexin's inner domain. Branch 1: a small switch protein turns off, and integrin feet loosen their grip on the substrate. Branch 2: other effectors act on actin filaments and microtubules. The two branches meet at a label: grip and actin lost.
scenes.narration: Inside, the plexin switches off a small GTPase of the Ras family. That protein helps integrins grip the surface. Other plexin pathways act on actin and microtubules. Together, the growth cone loses grip and actin.

scenes.tts: In a growth cone that Sema three A repels, where this happens shapes what you see. Typically, a gradient from one side turns it away, and a strong dose all round can fold the fan up, in preparations that support collapse.
scenes.visual: Header: a growth cone that Sema3A repels, typical outcomes. Left: Sema3A gradient from one side, that side loosens, the growth cone turns away. Right: strong Sema3A everywhere, all sides loosen, the fan can collapse. Labels: turn; possible collapse; dose, exposure and cell state matter too.
scenes.narration: In a growth cone that Sema3A repels, where this happens shapes what you see. Typically, a gradient from one side turns it away, and a strong dose all round can fold the fan up, in preparations that support collapse.
scenes.caption: In a growth cone that Sema3A repels, where this happens shapes what you see. Typically, a gradient from one side turns it away, and a strong dose all round can fold the fan up, in preparations that support collapse.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: for Sema three A, the working receptor is neuropilin and plexin together. No pair, no answer in these experiments.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: for Sema3A, the working receptor is neuropilin and plexin together. No pair, no answer in these experiments.
scenes.visual: Takeaway on screen: for Sema3A, no neuropilin-plexin pair, no answer.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: for Sema3A, the working receptor is neuropilin and plexin together. No pair, no answer in these experiments.
